extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and practitioners working on peer review / automated reviewer-assignment systems (conference organizers, algorithm designers, operations researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic review of metrics, models, and comparisons used to evaluate reviewer-assignment algorithms and systems (conference/journal/project proposals). Focuses on performance metrics, fairness/quality criteria, computational measures, and constraint-handling used across empirical and simulated evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching degree
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used widely as a direct measure of how well reviewers match papers (appears across many studies; often an objective in GAP/ILP and heuristic algorithms). Compared across algorithms such as Hungarian algorithm, greedy, ILP, and topic/model-based methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Load variance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures variance in reviewers' loads (used to assess balance/fairness of assignment). Appears in comparisons of methods that aim to balance assignment load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise variance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variance in expertise across assigned reviewers or across papers; used to evaluate fairness/quality of expertise distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPU time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw computational resource/time usage for an algorithm; used to compare algorithm efficiency (e.g., ILP vs heuristics, parallel algorithms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferences of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Takes reviewer self-reported preferences / bids into account; used as an objective or as a baseline for comparison (compare proposed method vs. reviewers' preferences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Times of movement for reviewers to change venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Times of movement for reviewers to change venues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric capturing reviewer inconvenience or mobility when assignments change venues; used in some assignment contexts to quantify cost of reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generic timing metric reported throughout the literature for algorithmic efficiency comparisons (appears repeatedly across studies and datasets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree to which reviewer expertise covers the topic space of submissions; used as an objective in multi-aspect or coverage-based assignments and to compare methods (e.g., coverage vs similarity-sum objectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported confidence values (often reviewer confidence in their expertise on assigned papers); sometimes aggregated (see Average Confidence). Used as a quality indicator for assignment outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average confidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean of reviewers' confidence scores across assignments; used to compare algorithms and measure expected review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness of assignment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level fairness criterion used to evaluate assignments (local fairness, global fairness, balance across authors/papers). Methods like PeerReview4All, FAIRIR, and FAIRFLOW evaluate fairness metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts-of-interest-aware assignment / assignment comparison by conflict types
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment comparison by different types of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations that explicitly measure how algorithms handle conflicts of interest (e.g., reduction of conflict violations, assignment outcomes when COI constraints vary). Used to compare approaches that incorporate COI constraints vs. those that do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total cost
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective often used in min-cost flow / assignment formulations (monetary/transportational/penalty cost aggregated across assignments). Compared across ILP and heuristic methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean utility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Average utility (suitability/similarity/score) across assignments; used when utility-based objectives (e.g., utilitarian social welfare) are studied. Appears alongside inequality measures (Hoover, Gini).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hoover index
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inequality / concentration measure applied to workload or utility distributions; used to assess balance or disparity in assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gini index
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard inequality metric applied to workloads, paper scores, or utility distributions to quantify unfairness or imbalance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time consumption
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a performance metric (wall-clock or CPU); used to compare scalability/efficiency of algorithms across datasets and settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments under constraints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates ability of methods to satisfy hard/soft constraints (load caps, COI, k-loop-free, capacity limits); performance reported as feasibility rates or number of violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average computation time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean runtime across runs or seeds; used to summarize algorithm efficiency across datasets or experiment sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best optimal adaptive value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in some evolutionary/search metaheuristic comparisons as best (fitness) found; used in comparing genetic/ant-colony/tabu methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average optimal adaptive value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean of the optimal/adaptive values found across multiple runs of stochastic algorithms; used to compare robustness/stability of heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total workload of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum or distribution of review assignments across reviewers; used to check capacity utilization and workload balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy / Recall / Precision / F-score
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic classification/information-retrieval metrics applied when reviewer-paper matching is posed as a predicted-match problem (e.g., recommender-system evaluation of matching quality). Reported in studies comparing feature/model choices (VSM, ATM, LSI, TF-IDF, word2vec).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility degree
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree to which a reviewer is eligible for a paper (e.g., subject-matter eligibility, conflicts); used as a constraint measure or to evaluate assignment quality/feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the solution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level reported measure (may include suitability scores, constraint satisfaction, or composite measures); often used in comparisons between ILP and heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time to compute an assignment (interactive latency) or time until reviewers respond; used in algorithm comparisons and operational evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimality ratio
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratio comparing heuristic solution value to known optimal (or oracle) solution; used when optimal ILP solutions are available for small/medium instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superiority ratio
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative metric used in some studies to quantify how much better one method is versus another (often in objective value or time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and rationality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composite notions used to describe assignment fairness and sensible distribution (appears in performance-metrics lists assessing fairness and distribution properties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time required to produce the full assignment (distinct from per-run computation time or initialization); used to measure practical deployability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialization time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time required to prepare data structures/models before search/assignment; relevant for methods with heavy preprocessing (topic models, similarity matrices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on avoiding the interest conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect on avoiding the interest conflict
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure of how well an algorithm reduces assignments that create conflicts of interest (an operational fairness/ethical metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness degree
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used in evolutionary/heuristic algorithms as the objective/fitness value for candidate assignments; reported for comparing metaheuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research intensity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proxy measures of reviewer expertise/activity level (e.g., publication counts) used to weight or evaluate assignments; affects assignment quality and load allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic association
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors such as co-authorship or institutional ties used in eligibility/COI modeling and in evaluating assignment safety/fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total suitability score
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate suitability (similarity) measure summed over all paper-reviewer pairs in the assignment; common objective in similarity-sum formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper bounds (on objective/performance)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported upper bounds on objective values or performance metrics used to contextualize algorithm outputs (e.g., in branch-and-bound/ILP experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: k-loop free assignment (k-loop-free constraint satisfaction)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constraint property ensuring no short review-exchange loops (k-loop free); used as a fairness/collusion-prevention criterion and operational constraint in some algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum of scores
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate of review scores (used as a quality metric for the review process or to compare assignment effects on score distributions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean of rating levels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Average reviewer ratings (used to assess assignment impact on review outcomes or to stratify reviewers by reliability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratios of standard deviations of rating percentages to the mean
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratios of standard deviations of rating percentages to the mean
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dispersion metric applied to rating distributions used to assess variability/consistency across reviewer ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraction of agents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proportion of reviewers or papers meeting a criterion (e.g., fraction of agents assigned, fraction satisfied); used in operational/completeness evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oracle optimal solution's similarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarity value of an oracle/optimal matching used as a benchmark to compute gaps for heuristics/approximation ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average assignment value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean suitability/similarity per assigned reviewer-paper pair; used to compare per-assignment quality across methods/datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilitarian social welfare
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum of utilities across agents/papers (classic welfare objective) used to evaluate aggregate matching quality; compared with egalitarian or Nash objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nash social welfare
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product (or log-sum) based social-welfare objective balancing efficiency and fairness; reported in comparative studies of welfare-optimal assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of EF1 Violations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count of envy-freeness up to one item violations across papers/reviewers; used to quantify fairness violations in allocation-based formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum paper score
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lowest paper score under an assignment (used to evaluate worst-off papers and to design min-max or egalitarian objectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Run time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General runtime metric (same family as computation/wall time) reported across experiments for scalability comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum of the envy across all paper pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of the envy across all paper pairs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate envy measure quantifying fairness of assignment outcomes; used to compare fairness-aware algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gini coefficient of all paper scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Gini coefficient of all paper scores
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inequality measure applied to final paper scores to evaluate equity of scoring outcomes induced by assignment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total similarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum of similarity/suitability scores over assigned pairs — common objective and reported metric comparing matching algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review score
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric review outcome (often used as a downstream quality indicator to see how assignment affects decision-related scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence of reviewer (percent)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentage or share expressing reviewer confidence; can be aggregated to Average Confidence and used to assess assignment-match quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of soft constraint violations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured decrease in number of violated soft constraints when using constraint-aware algorithms; used to compare single-phase vs multi-phase or soft-vs-hard constraint approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wall time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elapsed real time for an algorithm to finish (used alongside CPU time and number of iterations to report scalability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of iterations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteration counts for iterative/stochastic algorithms (used to compare convergence speed and computational effort).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of papers (as experimental axis)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an axis for scalability experiments (running time, solution quality vs. conference size); used to compare algorithms' scaling behavior.
